page: Microsoft Azure FX16ms_v2 is a compute-focused and memory-intensive virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server features 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a substantial 260 MB L3 cache, along with vector and matrix acceleration extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8). It is equipped with 336.0 GB of system memory, providing 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring remote managed disks for persistent storage.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded compute and instruction execution. The processor achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2143.0 and displays strong performance in compression benchmarks, reaching 34.37 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 14.22 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Text processing reaches the top tier at 2983.0 points in Geekbench. In LLM benchmarks, text generation on a small 135M model delivers top-tier performance at 415.01 tokens/sec, while prompt processing and multi-threaded throughput (such as 12947.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 17770.48 in multi-core stress-ng) track within average tiers. Large block memory bandwidth registers 81.55 GB/sec read and 47.78 GB/sec write.

A key architectural tradeoff for the FX16ms_v2 is its high memory capacity paired with a moderate core count, alongside the complete absence of local ephemeral storage. While its single-core clock frequency and high memory allocation make it cost-efficient for license-bound or memory-heavy applications, general memory access latency metrics like the PassMark memory score rank in the lower quartile. The instance is suited for electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, and compute jobs requiring high memory per core.
